chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdullah al-Mu'min, from Abd al-A'la, mawla of the family of Sam, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'By Allah, I indeed know the Book of Allah from its beginning to its end, as if it were in my palm. In it is the news of the heaven, the news of the earth, the news of what has been, and the news of what is to be.'
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'In it is the clarification of everything.'

key_terms.تِبْيَانُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ: clarification of everything, indicating the Qur'an’s all-encompassing explanatory nature
key_terms.خَبَرُ السَّمَاءِ: the news of the heaven, referring to knowledge of heavenly matters
key_terms.خَبَرُ الْأَرْضِ: the news of the earth, referring to knowledge of earthly matters
key_terms.فِي كَفِّي: in my palm, expressing total clarity and immediacy of knowledge
key_terms.كِتَابَ اللَّهِ: the Book of Allah, meaning the Qur'an in its entirety
key_terms.مَا كَانَ: what has been, meaning past realities and events
key_terms.مَا هُوَ كَائِنٌ: what is to be, meaning future occurrences
key_terms.مِنْ أَوَّلِهِ إِلَى آخِرِهِ: from its beginning to its end, indicating complete knowledge

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe Imam al-Sadiq’s عليه السلام knowledge of the Qur'an?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms the comprehensive knowledge of Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام regarding the Book of Allah and presents the Qur'an as containing clarification of all things. It highlights, in Shia understanding, the special authority of the Imams عليهم السلام in possessing complete knowledge of the Qur'an and its realities.
